text:
William Stromgren needed only five games to score twice in the NHL. The 23-year-old Swede, a 2021 second-round pick who had gone pointless in three games last season, scored his first NHL goal against San Jose on Nov. 2, then opened the scoring against Anaheim's Lukas Dostal four days later. He plays bottom-six minutes, a little over nine a night, after a 49-point season with the AHL Calgary Wranglers in 2024-25.

Five games is a tiny sample, and it should be read that way. Two goals on four shots is a 50% shooting rate, which no one keeps, though his chances (0.88 expected goals, our measure of shot quality) have been decent for the minutes. The early on-ice signs are encouraging: Calgary has taken 56% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, more than nine points better than without him. Our range for him over a full season is wide, 6 to 16 goals, which is honest about how little we know yet. What to watch is whether the Flames keep finding him minutes once the puck stops going in on every other shot.
headline: William Stromgren's fast start comes with a small sample
